newsitem.title: USA: Man gets prison for defrauding Barclays.
newsitem.headline: Man gets prison for defrauding Barclays.

text.p: A former analyst at M.D. Sass Investor Services was sentenced to six years in prison Wednesday for defrauding Barclays Bank of some $13 million to buy more than 30 cars, homes and expensive electronics.
Trevor Hunt, 31, was also ordered by U.S. District Judge Shira Scheindlin to make full restitution. He has repaid more than $5 million and must still pay over $8.1 million.
In sentencing Hunt, Scheindlin said the defendant "was motivated soley by greed rather than need" and that he spent the funds "for his own enjoyment."

Hunt used the money to buy about 30 cars, including a Porsche, a Lamborghini, a Jaguar and several Grand Prix racing cars. He also bought several homes, expensive clothing and electronic equipment, the complaint charged.
The judge said there were no mitigating factors to reduce the prison term such as good works done for the community or family obligations.

Scheindlin said Hunt would be 37 and still a young man when released from prison. She said he was obviously bright enough to carry out the complex scheme and encouraged him to concentrate on legitimate ways to make money while incarcerated.
Before sentencing, Hunt apologised for his crimes and described them as "self-serving."
"I thought only of myself. I take full responsibility for my crimes and there's no way I can make up for what I've done."
Hunt's attorney, Francis Murray, told the judge his client had been living two lives. He described Hunt as a race car driver who had been running a separate race car business.

Hunt pleaded guilty in October to one count of bank fraud for carrying out the scheme between January 1994 and August 1996. He admitted obtaining millions of dollars of funds from Barclays that belonged to Sass and its clients

Hunt had been a performance analyst at Sass, an investment advisory firm, and was responsible for communicating with the investment firms and banks at which funds belonging to Sass' clients were held.

His job included instructing investment firms to transfer clients' funds to Barclays Bank, a unit of Barclays Plc, where Sass kept clients' funds on a short-term basis while they were either being transferred to the client or to another type of investment.
Hunt was also responsible for telling Barclays where to transfer funds.

Hunt initially told investment firms to transfer funds belonging to Sass clients to Barclays on the false pretense that the full amount of those funds was being sought by clients. He then told Barclays to wire the amount into Sass's business accounts held at Citibank by Bear, Stearns & Co.
In doing so, he falsely represented to Barclays that the funds to be transferred would be used for Sass and its customers.
The complaint charged that Hunt used forged and false documents to get Bear Stearns to transfer funds from Sass' business accounts to accounts that Hunt owned or controlled.
